nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the Fibonacci factorial $F_n!$ is a nonzero rational number.
nodes.title: Fibonacci factorials are nonzero

nodes.summary: The Fibonacci factorial $F_1!$ equals $1$, since the first Fibonacci number is $F_1 = 1$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci factorial at one

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the Fibonacci factorial $F_n!$ is a strictly positive rational number.
nodes.title: Fibonacci factorials are positive

nodes.summary: The Fibonacci factorial $F_3! = F_1 F_2 F_3$ of the Fibonacci numbers $F_1, F_2, F_3$ equals $2$, since $F_1 = F_2 = 1$ and $F_3 = 2$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci factorial at three

nodes.summary: The Fibonacci factorial $F_2! = F_1 F_2$ of the Fibonacci numbers $F_1, F_2$ equals $1$, since $F_1 = F_2 = 1$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci factorial at two

nodes.summary: The Fibonacci factorial $F_0!$ equals $1$, by the empty-product convention.
nodes.title: Fibonacci factorial at zero

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Fibonacci factorial $F_n!$ is the rational number $F_n! = F_1 F_2 \cdots F_n$, the product of the first $n$ Fibonacci numbers (where $F_1 = F_2 = 1$ and $F_{k+2} = F_{k+1} + F_k$); in particular $F_0! = 1$, the empty product.
nodes.title: Fibonacci factorial

nodes.summary: For every natural number $r$, the Jordan-type quotient $J_{r,F} = F_{2r+1}! / F_r!$ of Fibonacci factorials is a strictly positive rational number.
nodes.title: Fibonacci Jordan quotient is positive

nodes.summary: The Jordan-type quotient $J_{r,F} = F_{2r+1}! / F_r!$ of Fibonacci factorials takes the value $J_{0,F} = F_1! / F_0! = 1$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci Jordan quotient at zero

nodes.summary: The Jordan-type quotient $J_{r,F} = F_{2r+1}! / F_r!$ of Fibonacci factorials takes the value $J_{1,F} = F_3! / F_1! = 2$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci Jordan quotient at one

nodes.summary: For a natural number $r$, the Jordan-type quotient is the rational number $J_{r,F} = F_{2r+1}! / F_r!$, where $F_m! = F_1 F_2 \cdots F_m$ is the Fibonacci factorial of the Fibonacci numbers $F_1 = F_2 = 1$, $F_{k+2} = F_{k+1} + F_k$ (so $F_0! = 1$).
nodes.title: Fibonacci Jordan quotient

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the fibonomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}_F$ is the rational number $F_n!/(F_k! \, F_{n-k}!)$ when $k \le n$, where $F_i$ is the $i$-th Fibonacci number and $F_j! = F_1 F_2 \cdots F_j$ is the Fibonacci factorial, and $0$ when $k > n$.
nodes.title: Fibonomial coefficients

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r$ and $n$, the generalized FiboCatalan number with parameters $r$ and $n$ is a positive integer: it equals $k$ for some natural number $k \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Generalized FiboCatalan numbers are positive integers

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r$ and $n$, the generalized FiboCatalan number with parameters $r$ and $n$ is a strictly positive rational number.
nodes.title: Positivity of generalized FiboCatalan numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the generalized FiboCatalan number with parameters $r = 0$ and $n$ equals the FiboCatalan number $F_{2n}! / (F_n! \, F_{n+1}!)$, where $F_i$ is the $i$-th Fibonacci number ($F_1 = F_2 = 1$) and $F_m! = F_1 F_2 \cdots F_m$ is the Fibonacci factorial (with $F_0! = 1$).
nodes.title: Generalized FiboCatalan numbers at r = 0

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the generalized FiboCatalan number with parameters $r = 1$ and $n$ equals $2 F_{2n}! / (F_{n+2}! \, F_n!)$, where $F_i$ is the $i$-th Fibonacci number ($F_1 = F_2 = 1$) and $F_m! = F_1 F_2 \cdots F_m$ is the Fibonacci factorial (with $F_0! = 1$).
nodes.title: Generalized FiboCatalan numbers at r = 1

nodes.summary: Let $F_m! = F_1 F_2 \cdots F_m$ denote the Fibonacci factorial of the Fibonacci numbers $F_1 = F_2 = 1$, $F_{k+2} = F_{k+1} + F_k$ (so $F_0! = 1$), and let $J_{r,F} = F_{2r+1}! / F_r!$ be the Fibonacci Jordan quotient. For natural numbers $r$ and $n$, the generalized FiboCatalan number with parameters $r$ and $n$ is the rational number $J_{r,F} \, F_{2n}! / (F_n! \, F_{n+r+1}!)$.
nodes.title: Generalized FiboCatalan numbers

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Lucas factorial $\{n\}!$ is the product $\{n\}! = \{1\}\{2\} \cdots \{n\}$ of the Lucas polynomials $\{i\}$ in $s$ and $t$ for $1 \le i \le n$, a polynomial with integer coefficients; in particular $\{0\}! = 1$, the empty product.
nodes.title: Lucas factorial

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the $k$-divisible Lucas factorial $\{n : k\}!$ is the product $\{n : k\}! = \{k\}\{2k\} \cdots \{nk\}$ of the Lucas polynomials $\{ki\}$ in $s$ and $t$ for $1 \le i \le n$; in particular $\{0 : k\}! = 1$, the empty product.
nodes.title: $k$-divisible Lucas factorial

nodes.title: Cross-product identity for Lucas polynomials

nodes.summary: The Lucas polynomials $\{n\}$, for natural numbers $n$, are the polynomials in two variables $s$ and $t$ with integer coefficients defined by $\{0\} = 0$, $\{1\} = 1$ and $\{n + 2\} = s\{n + 1\} + t\{n\}$ for every $n \ge 0$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
